candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

candidates.label: isTierOf
candidates.comment: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.

candidates.label: studentOf
candidates.comment: Indicates the educational institution where a person is a student.

candidates.label: hasTierRequirement
candidates.comment: A tier requirement relation between a member program tier and a condition for joining that tier. Also called tier eligibility, membership condition, joining requirement. Examples: "A member program tier has a tier requirement of a specific credit card.", "The tier has a tier requirement of a minimum spend.", "This tier requires a tier requirement of an annual fee."

candidates.label: belongsToCountry
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity belongs to or is associated with a specific country.

art4.query: beat: Indicates that one competitor defeated another in a contest.

candidates.label: beat
candidates.comment: Indicates that one sports team defeated another in a contest.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: wonEvent
candidates.comment: Indicates the sports event that a person or team won.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: hasPrizeForRank
candidates.comment: Indicates the competition rank for which prize money is distributed.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: hasCategory
candidates.comment: Indicates a specific category or division associated with an entity, such as a prize money distribution.

art4.query: participated in: Indicates that an entity took part in an event or activity.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: observed
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity observed something.

candidates.label: celebrates
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity is observing or commemorating an event.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: occursDuring
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period within which an entity occurs or is valid.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: wonEvent
candidates.comment: Indicates the sports event that a person or team won.

candidates.label: activeOnDate
candidates.comment: Indicates the date on which an entity was active or present.

candidates.label: occursDuringPeriod
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period during which an event occurs or is valid.

art5.query: about: Indicates the primary subject or topic of an event or claim.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: states
candidates.comment: Indicates the content or assertion made in a claim or creative work.

candidates.label: hasSource
candidates.comment: Indicates the origin or provider of a claim or information.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: hasCategory
candidates.comment: Indicates a specific category or division associated with an entity, such as a prize money distribution.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: occursDuring
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period within which an entity occurs or is valid.

candidates.label: celebrates
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity is observing or commemorating an event.

art5.query: locatedIn: Indicates the geographical location where something is situated or an event takes place.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: originatesFromLocation
candidates.comment: Indicates the geographical starting point from which something is developing or increasing.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: availableIn
candidates.comment: An administrative area where a drug strength is available. Also called: market availability, regional availability. Examples: "DrugStrength '500mg' availableIn 'US'", "DrugStrength '10mg' availableIn 'EU'."

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

art5.query: hasSource: Indicates the origin or provider of information, a statement, or a report.

candidates.label: hasSource
candidates.comment: Indicates the origin or provider of a claim or information.

candidates.label: hasDescriptor
candidates.comment: Indicates a characteristic or quality attributed to an entity.

candidates.label: hasEnabler
candidates.comment: Indicates a factor or resource that makes something possible for an entity.

candidates.label: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails
candidates.comment: An energy consumption detail relation between a product and its energy efficiency information. Also called energy efficiency details, energy rating details, consumption specifics. Examples: "A refrigerator has energy consumption details.", "An appliance has energy consumption details for its class.", "The product's energy consumption details are listed."

candidates.label: hasAlert
candidates.comment: Indicates that an alert or warning has been issued or is in effect for an entity.

candidates.label: hasRecipient
candidates.comment: Indicates the entity that receives something from an action.

candidates.label: hasCharacteristic
candidates.comment: Indicates a distinguishing quality or feature of an entity.

candidates.label: hasRiskFactor
candidates.comment: Indicates a potential danger or negative outcome associated with an event or situation.

candidates.label: hasCourseInstance
candidates.comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. Examples: "A calculus course has a course instance for Fall 2023.", "The online course has a course instance for self-paced study.", "A cooking class has a course instance on Tuesdays at 6 PM."

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

art5.query: reports: Indicates that a source provides information or details about a subject.

candidates.label: reportedTo
candidates.comment: Indicates the entity to whom information was conveyed or reported.

candidates.label: states
candidates.comment: Indicates the content or assertion made in a claim or creative work.

candidates.label: reportsRestrictionTo
candidates.comment: Indicates that a report states a limitation or confinement to a specific geographical area.

candidates.label: hasSource
candidates.comment: Indicates the origin or provider of a claim or information.

candidates.label: observed
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity observed something.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: chronicled
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity recorded or documented something.

candidates.label: studies
candidates.comment: Indicates the academic subject or field of study a person pursues.

candidates.label: provides
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity offers or makes available something.

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

art5.query: partOf: Indicates that one entity or event is a component or segment of another larger entity or event.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: containsPart
candidates.comment: Indicates that an entity contains a component or section.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

art5.query: hasParticipant: None

candidates.label: hasRecipient
candidates.comment: Indicates the entity that receives something from an action.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: doesNotShip
candidates.comment: A does not ship relation between offer shipping details, shipping conditions, or shipping rate settings and a boolean value indicating when shipping to a particular destination is unavailable. Also called "shipping unavailable", "no shipping to", "delivery excluded". Examples: "Offer shipping details doesNotShip 'true' for Alaska", "Shipping conditions doesNotShip 'true' for international orders", "Shipping rate settings doesNotShip 'true' for PO boxes".

candidates.label: hasRiskFactor
candidates.comment: Indicates a potential danger or negative outcome associated with an event or situation.

candidates.label: hasCategory
candidates.comment: Indicates a specific category or division associated with an entity, such as a prize money distribution.

candidates.label: hasLabel
candidates.comment: Indicates a label or identifying text associated with an entity.

candidates.label: hasAge
candidates.comment: Indicates the age or duration of existence of an entity.

candidates.label: hasVariant
candidates.comment: A product variant relation between a product group and a specific product that is a variant within that group. Also called product variation, variant of, member of group. Examples: "A product group has a variant for a different color.", "The product model has a variant for a larger size.", "This group includes a product variant."

art5.query: atTime: Indicates the specific time or period when an event or claim occurs or is made.

candidates.label: occursDuringPeriod
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period during which an event occurs or is valid.

candidates.label: occursDuring
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period within which an entity occurs or is valid.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: presentDuringPeriod
candidates.comment: Indicates the time period during which an entity was present or installed.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: departedAtTime
candidates.comment: Indicates the time at which an entity departed.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

art5.query: isTitleOf: Indicates the official position or role held by a person within an organization.

candidates.label: isTierOf
candidates.comment: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.

candidates.label: isHeadquartersOf
candidates.comment: Indicates that a building or place serves as the primary administrative center for an organization.

candidates.label: isFanOf
candidates.comment: Indicates that a person is a supporter or admirer of another person or entity.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: studentOf
candidates.comment: Indicates the educational institution where a person is a student.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: hasRole
candidates.comment: Indicates the function or part played by a person.

art5.query: relatedTo: Indicates a general connection or association between two entities.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: comparedTo
candidates.comment: Indicates a comparison between two entities or values.

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: reportedTo
candidates.comment: Indicates the entity to whom information was conveyed or reported.
